claim: HIV and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infections are known for impaired neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses.
source: HIV and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infections are known for impaired neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses.

claim: Sequential virus–host B cell interaction appears to be basally required for NAb induction.
source: While sequential virus–host B cell interaction appears to be basally required for NAb induction, driver molecular signatures predisposing to NAb induction still remain largely unknown.
evidence: This statement is presented as an established understanding in the field, though the manuscript notes that specific molecular drivers remain unknown.

claim: Driver molecular signatures predisposing to NAb induction still remain largely unknown.
source: While sequential virus–host B cell interaction appears to be basally required for NAb induction, driver molecular signatures predisposing to NAb induction still remain largely unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Screening of seventy difficult-to-neutralize SIVmac239-infected macaques found nine NAb-inducing animals.
source: Screening of seventy difficult-to-neutralize SIVmac239-infected macaques found nine NAb-inducing animals, with seven selecting for a specific CD8+ T-cell escape mutation in viral nef before NAb induction.
evidence: This is a direct report of the experimental findings from the screening study.

claim: Seven of the nine NAb-inducing animals selected for a specific CD8+ T-cell escape mutation in viral nef before NAb induction.
source: Screening of seventy difficult-to-neutralize SIVmac239-infected macaques found nine NAb-inducing animals, with seven selecting for a specific CD8+ T-cell escape mutation in viral nef before NAb induction.
evidence: This is a key finding from the data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation reduced excess Nef interaction-mediated drive of B-cell maturation-limiting PI3K/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2).
source: This Nef-G63E mutation reduced excess Nef interaction-mediated drive of B-cell maturation-limiting PI3K/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2).
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: In vivo imaging cytometry depicted preferential Nef perturbation of cognate Envelope-specific B cells.
source: In vivo imaging cytometry depicted preferential Nef perturbation of cognate Envelope-specific B cells, suggestive of polarized contact-dependent Nef transfer and corroborating cognate B-cell maturation post-mutant selection up to NAb induction.
evidence: This is a finding from the imaging cytometry experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: The preferential Nef perturbation of Envelope-specific B cells is suggestive of polarized contact-dependent Nef transfer.
source: In vivo imaging cytometry depicted preferential Nef perturbation of cognate Envelope-specific B cells, suggestive of polarized contact-dependent Nef transfer and corroborating cognate B-cell maturation post-mutant selection up to NAb induction.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the imaging cytometry data.

claim: The findings corroborate cognate B-cell maturation post-mutant selection up to NAb induction.
source: In vivo imaging cytometry depicted preferential Nef perturbation of cognate Envelope-specific B cells, suggestive of polarized contact-dependent Nef transfer and corroborating cognate B-cell maturation post-mutant selection up to NAb induction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental findings.

claim: The NAb induction pattern is extrinsically reciprocal to human PI3K gain-of-function antibody-dysregulating disease.
source: Results collectively exemplify a NAb induction pattern extrinsically reciprocal to human PI3K gain-of-function antibody-dysregulating disease and indicate that harnessing the PI3K/mTORC2 axis may facilitate NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV.
evidence: This is an interpretation comparing the findings to known human disease mechanisms.

claim: Harnessing the PI3K/mTORC2 axis may facilitate NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV.
source: Results collectively exemplify a NAb induction pattern extrinsically reciprocal to human PI3K gain-of-function antibody-dysregulating disease and indicate that harnessing the PI3K/mTORC2 axis may facilitate NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: Virus-specific neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses by B cells are induced by an intricate cooperation of adaptive immune cells.
source: Virus-specific neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses by B cells are induced by an intricate cooperation of adaptive immune cells (Kumar et al., 2010; Shulman et al., 2014; Gitlin et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014) and often play a central role in clearance of acute viral infections (Junt et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: NAb responses often play a central role in clearance of acute viral infections.
source: Virus-specific neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses by B cells are induced by an intricate cooperation of adaptive immune cells (Kumar et al., 2010; Shulman et al., 2014; Gitlin et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014) and often play a central role in clearance of acute viral infections (Junt et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Persistence-prone viruses such as HIV-1, SIV, and LCMV variously equip themselves with B cell/antibody-inhibitory countermeasures.
source: In contrast, persistence-prone viruses such as human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV), and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) variously equip themselves with B cell/antibody-inhibitory countermeasures (Moir et al., 2001; Mattapallil et al., 2005; Sommerstein et al., 2015; Sammicheli et al., 2016; Fallet et al., 2016; Mason et al., 2016), impairing NAb induction (Levesque et al., 2009; Mikell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: B cell/antibody-inhibitory countermeasures of persistence-prone viruses impair NAb induction.
source: In contrast, persistence-prone viruses such as human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV), and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) variously equip themselves with B cell/antibody-inhibitory countermeasures (Moir et al., 2001; Mattapallil et al., 2005; Sommerstein et al., 2015; Sammicheli et al., 2016; Fallet et al., 2016; Mason et al., 2016), impairing NAb induction (Levesque et al., 2009; Mikell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: HIV and SIV successfully suppress elicitation of potent NAb responses, especially in acute infection.
source: These viruses successfully suppress elicitation of potent NAb responses, especially in acute infection (Hunziker et al., 2003; Tomaras et al., 2008), and establish viral persistence, posing considerable challenges for developing protective strategies.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: HIV and SIV establish viral persistence, posing considerable challenges for developing protective strategies.
source: These viruses successfully suppress elicitation of potent NAb responses, especially in acute infection (Hunziker et al., 2003; Tomaras et al., 2008), and establish viral persistence, posing considerable challenges for developing protective strategies.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field.

claim: HIV and SIV establish early a large body of infection in vivo with a distinct host genome-integrating retroviral life cycle.
source: In particular, HIV and SIV establish early a large body of infection in vivo from early on with a distinct host genome-integrating retroviral life cycle (Whitney et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: HIV and SIV lentiviruses are unique in launching a matrix of host immune-perturbing interactions mainly by their six remarkably pleiotropic accessory viral proteins.
source: In addition, these lentiviruses are unique in launching a matrix of host immune-perturbing interactions mainly by their six remarkably pleiotropic accessory viral proteins, which optimally fuels viral pathogenesis (Kirchhoff et al., 1995; Sheehy et al., 2002; Harris et al., 2003; Schindler et al., 2006; Neil et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2009; Laguette et al., 2011; Yamada et al., 2018; Joas et al., 2018; Langer et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2019; Joas et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2020; Volcic et al., 2020; Reuschl et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The pleiotropic accessory viral proteins optimally fuel viral pathogenesis.
source: In addition, these lentiviruses are unique in launching a matrix of host immune-perturbing interactions mainly by their six remarkably pleiotropic accessory viral proteins, which optimally fuels viral pathogenesis (Kirchhoff et al., 1995; Sheehy et al., 2002; Harris et al., 2003; Schindler et al., 2006; Neil et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2009; Laguette et al., 2011; Yamada et al., 2018; Joas et al., 2018; Langer et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2019; Joas et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2020; Volcic et al., 2020; Reuschl et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Focal mechanisms of humoral immune perturbation in HIV/SIV infection remain elusive to date.
source: A body of evidence has depicted this in the last decades, whereas its entity, including focal mechanisms of humoral immune perturbation in HIV/SIV infection, remains elusive to date.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Adverse virus–host interactions in HIV/SIV infection lead to a detrimental consequence of the absence of acute-phase endogenous NAb responses.
source: Adverse virus–host interactions in HIV/SIV infection lead to a detrimental consequence of the absence of acute-phase endogenous NAb responses.
evidence: This is a summary of established knowledge in the field.

claim: Passive NAb infusion in the acute phase can trigger an endogenous T-cell synergism, resulting in robust control of SIV and chimeric SHIV.
source: Contrasting this, we and others have previously described in in vivo experimental models that passive NAb infusion in the acute phase can trigger an endogenous T-cell synergism, resulting in robust control of SIV and chimeric SHIV (simian/human immunodeficiency virus) (Haigwood et al., 1996; Yamamoto et al., 2007; Ng et al., 2010; Iseda et al., 2016; Nishimura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research, including the authors' own work.

claim: Virus-specific NAbs not only confer sterile protection but also can evoke T-cell-mediated non-sterile viral control.
source: This indicates that virus-specific NAbs not only confer sterile protection but also can evoke T-cell-mediated non-sterile viral control, suggesting the importance of endogenous NAb responses supported by humoral-cellular response synergisms, during an optimal time frame.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited prior research.

claim: Endogenous NAb responses supported by humoral-cellular response synergisms during an optimal time frame are important.
source: This indicates that virus-specific NAbs not only confer sterile protection but also can evoke T-cell-mediated non-sterile viral control, suggesting the importance of endogenous NAb responses supported by humoral-cellular response synergisms, during an optimal time frame.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited prior research.

claim: Identifying the mechanisms driving NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses is an important step to eventually design NAb-based HIV control strategies.
source: Therefore, identifying the mechanisms driving NAb induction against such viruses is an important step to eventually design NAb-based HIV control strategies.
evidence: This is a logical conclusion based on the importance of NAb responses.

claim: Analysis of in vivo immunological events linked with NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize SIVs in a non-human primate model can provide important insights.
source: One approach that can provide important insights into this goal is the analysis of in vivo immunological events linked with NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize SIVs in a non-human primate model.
evidence: This is the rationale for the study's approach.

claim: Various in vivo signatures of HIV-specific NAb induction, such as antibody-NAb coevolution, autoimmune-driven induction, and natural killer cell-related host polymorphisms, have been reported to date.
source: Various in vivo signatures of HIV-specific NAb induction, such as antibody-NAb coevolution (Moore et al., 2012), autoimmune-driven induction (Moody et al., 2016), and natural killer cell-related host polymorphisms (Bradley et al., 2018), have been reported to date.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The broad range of contributing factors to NAb induction indicates that pathways to NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV are redundant.
source: The broad range of contributing factors collectively, and interestingly, indicates that pathways to NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV are redundant, and may potentially involve as-yet-unknown mechanisms driving NAb induction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the diversity of reported mechanisms.

claim: Pathways to NAb induction may potentially involve as-yet-unknown mechanisms.
source: The broad range of contributing factors collectively, and interestingly, indicates that pathways to NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV are redundant, and may potentially involve as-yet-unknown mechanisms driving NAb induction.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the diversity of known mechanisms.

claim: The neutralization resistance of certain SIV strains does not appear to be explained by any of the aforementioned mechanisms.
source: For example, the neutralization resistance of certain SIV strains does not appear to be explained by any of the aforementioned, posing SIV models as attractive tools to analyze NAb induction mechanisms.
evidence: This is an observation that motivates the use of SIV models.

claim: SIV models are attractive tools to analyze NAb induction mechanisms.
source: For example, the neutralization resistance of certain SIV strains does not appear to be explained by any of the aforementioned, posing SIV models as attractive tools to analyze NAb induction mechanisms.
evidence: This is the rationale for using SIV models in this study.

claim: SIVmac239 is pathogenic in rhesus macaques causing simian AIDS across a broad range of geographical origin of macaques.
source: This virus is pathogenic in rhesus macaques causing simian AIDS across a broad range of geographical origin of macaques (Cumont et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Macaques infected with SIVmac239 show persistent viremia and generally lack NAb responses throughout infection.
source: Macaques infected with SIVmac239 show persistent viremia and generally lack NAb responses throughout infection (Kestler et al., 1991; Nomura et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A large-scale screening of SIVmac239-infected Burmese rhesus macaques for up to 100 weeks identified a subgroup inducing NAbs in the chronic phase.
source: In this study, a large-scale screening of SIVmac239-infected Burmese rhesus macaques for up to 100 weeks identified a subgroup inducing NAbs in the chronic phase.
evidence: This is a direct report of the study's findings.

claim: Before NAb induction, NAb-inducing animals commonly selected for a specific CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) escape mutation in the viral Nef-coding gene.
source: Interestingly, before NAb induction, these animals commonly selected for a specific CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) escape mutation in the viral Nef-coding gene.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study's data analysis.

claim: The mutant Nef manifested a decrease in aberrant interaction with phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2), resulting in decreased downstream hyperactivation of the canonical B-cell negative regulator Akt.
source: Compared with wild-type (WT) Nef, this mutant Nef manifested a decrease in aberrant interaction with phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2), resulting in decreased downstream hyperactivation of the canonical B-cell negative regulator Akt (Omori et al., 2006; Limon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study, with citations supporting the role of Akt.

claim: Akt is a canonical B-cell negative regulator.
source: Compared with wild-type (WT) Nef, this mutant Nef manifested a decrease in aberrant interaction with phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2), resulting in decreased downstream hyperactivation of the canonical B-cell negative regulator Akt (Omori et al., 2006; Limon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Machine learning-assisted imaging cytometry revealed that Nef preferentially targets Env-specific B cells in vivo.
source: Machine learning-assisted imaging cytometry revealed that Nef preferentially targets Env-specific B cells in vivo.
evidence: This is a finding from the imaging cytometry experiments.

claim: The NAb induction was linked with sustained Env-specific B-cell responses after or during the mutant Nef selection.
source: Furthermore, the NAb induction was linked with sustained Env-specific B-cell responses after or during the mutant Nef selection.
evidence: This is a finding from the B-cell response analysis.

claim: NAb induction in SIVmac239-infected hosts conceivably involves a functional boosting of B cells that is phenotypically reciprocal to human PI3K gain-of-function and antibody-dysregulating inborn error of immunity (IEI), activated PI3 kinase delta syndrome (APDS).
source: Thus, NAb induction in SIVmac239-infected hosts conceivably involves a functional boosting of B cells that is phenotypically reciprocal to a recently found human PI3K gain-of-function and antibody-dysregulating inborn error of immunity (IEI), activated PI3 kinase delta syndrome (APDS) (Angulo et al., 2013; Lucas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of human disease, supported by citations.

claim: Intervening PI3K/mTORC2 signaling can potentially result in harnessing NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses.
source: Our results suggest that intervening PI3K/mTORC2 signaling can potentially result in harnessing NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: NAb inducers showed persistent viremia with no significant difference in viral loads compared with NAb non-inducers.
source: These NAb inducers showed persistent viremia with no significant difference in viral loads compared with a subgroup of NAb non-inducers (n = 19) that were previously profile-clarified, naïve, and major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) haplotype-balanced (used for comparison hereafter) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the viral load analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: Plasma SIVmac239-NAb titers showed an average maximum titer of 1:16, being induced at an average of 48 weeks post-infection.
source: Plasma SIVmac239-NAb titers measured by 10 TCID50 SIVmac239 virus-killing assay showed an average maximum titer of 1:16, being induced at an average of 48 weeks post-infection (p.i.) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct report of the NAb titer measurements.

claim: Two of the nine NAb inducers showed detectable NAb responses by 24 weeks p.i., while the remaining seven induced NAbs after 30 weeks p.i.
source: Two of the nine NAb inducers showed detectable NAb responses by 24 weeks p.i., while the remaining seven induced NAbs after 30 weeks p.i.
evidence: This is a direct report of the timing of NAb induction.

claim: Anti-SIVmac239 neutralizing activity was confirmed in immunoglobulin G (IgG) purified from plasma of NAb inducers.
source: Anti-SIVmac239 neutralizing activity was confirmed in immunoglobulin G (IgG) purified from plasma of these NAb inducers (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the IgG purification and neutralization assay.

claim: SIV Env-binding IgGs developed from early infection in both NAb inducers and non-rapid-progressing NAb non-inducers.
source: SIV Env-binding IgGs developed from early infection in both NAb inducers and non-rapid-progressing NAb non-inducers, the latter differing from rapid progressors known to manifest serological failure (Hirsch et al., 2004; Nakane et al., 2013; Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the Env-binding IgG analysis, with citations supporting the comparison to rapid progressors.

claim: Titers of Env-binding IgG were not higher but rather lower at year 1 p.i. in the NAb inducers.
source: Titers of Env-binding IgG were not higher but rather lower at year 1 p.i. in the NAb inducers (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the Env-binding IgG titer analysis.

claim: The lower Env-binding IgG titers in NAb inducers were consistent with other reports.
source: This was consistent with other reports (Havenar-Daughton et al., 2016) and differing with gross B-cell enhancement in Nef-deleted SIV infection with enhanced anti-SIV binding antibody titers accompanying marginal neutralization (Adnan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior research findings.

claim: NAb inducers and non-inducers showed similar patterns of variations in viral env sequences, mainly in variable regions 1, 2 and 4 (V1, V2, and V4).
source: NAb inducers and non-inducers showed similar patterns of variations in viral env sequences (Burns et al., 1993), mainly in variable regions 1, 2 and 4 (V1, V2, and V4) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the viral sequence analysis.

claim: Selection of a viral genome mutation resulting in G (glycine)-to-E (glutamic acid) substitution at residue 63 of Nef (Nef-G63E) was found in seven of the nine NAb inducers.
source: Strikingly, we found selection of a viral genome mutation resulting in G (glycine)-to-E (glutamic acid) substitution at residue 63 of Nef (Nef-G63E) in seven of the nine NAb inducers (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a key finding from the viral genome sequencing.

claim: Two inducers that did not select Nef-G63E were the early inducers detected for NAb positivity before 24 weeks p.i.
source: Two inducers that did not select Nef-G63E were the early inducers detected for NAb positivity before 24 weeks p.i.
evidence: This is an observation from the data analysis.

claim: The 63rd residue of Nef lies in the unstructured N-terminus, flanked by two α-helices conserved in SIVmac/SIVsmm.
source: This 63rd residue lies in the unstructured N-terminus of Nef, flanked by two α-helices conserved in SIVmac/SIVsmm (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a structural characterization of the mutation site.

claim: The region containing the 63rd residue of Nef is generally polymorphic among HIV-1/HIV-2/SIV, occasionally being deleted in laboratory and primary isolate HIV-1 strains.
source: This region is generally polymorphic among HIV-1/HIV-2/SIV, occasionally being deleted in laboratory and primary isolate HIV-1 strains (Geyer et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: AlphaFold2-based structure prediction did not derive palpable change except for low-probability disruption of the alpha helices.
source: AlphaFold2-based structure prediction did not derive palpable change except for low-probability disruption of the alpha helices (data not shown).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural prediction analysis.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation was found only in 2 of the 19 NAb non-inducers, including one rapid progressor.
source: This mutation was found only in 2 of the 19 NAb non-inducers, including one rapid progressor (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and selection was significantly enriched in the NAb inducers compared to the 19 non-inducers (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of NAb inducers and non-inducers.

claim: Nef-G63E selection was significantly enriched in the NAb inducers compared to the 19 non-inducers.
source: This mutation was found only in 2 of the 19 NAb non-inducers, including one rapid progressor (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and selection was significantly enriched in the NAb inducers compared to the 19 non-inducers (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the comparative analysis.

claim: Analysis of Nef-G63E mutation frequencies in plasma viruses showed that Nef-G63E selection preceded or at least paralleled NAb induction.
source: Analysis of Nef-G63E mutation frequencies in plasma viruses showed that Nef-G63E selection preceded or at least paralleled NAb induction (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the temporal analysis of mutation frequencies.

claim: The seven NAb inducers selecting the Nef-G63E mutation elicited CD8+ T-cell responses specific for a 9-mer peptide Nef62–70 QW9 (QGQYMNTPW).
source: We found that these seven NAb inducers selecting this mutation elicited CD8+ T-cell responses specific for a 9-mer peptide Nef62–70 QW9 (QGQYMNTPW) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the CD8+ T-cell response analysis.

claim: The Nef62–70 QW9 epitope is restricted by MHC-I molecules Mamu-B*004:01 and Mamu-B*039:01.
source: This Nef62–70 QW9 epitope is restricted by MHC-I molecules Mamu-B*004:01 and Mamu-B*039:01 (Evans et al., 1999; Sette et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Possession of Mamu-B*004:01 and Mamu-B*039:01 accounted for six cases of Nef-G63E selection.
source: Possession of these accounted for six cases of Nef-G63E selection (Figure 3A), and the remaining one animal possessed Mamu-A1*032:02 predicted to bind to Nef63–70 GW8 (NetMHCpan).
evidence: This is a finding from the MHC-I genotype analysis.

claim: The remaining one animal possessed Mamu-A1*032:02 predicted to bind to Nef63–70 GW8.
source: Possession of these accounted for six cases of Nef-G63E selection (Figure 3A), and the remaining one animal possessed Mamu-A1*032:02 predicted to bind to Nef63–70 GW8 (NetMHCpan).
evidence: This is a finding from the MHC-I genotype analysis and binding prediction.

claim: 10 of 19 NAb non-inducers also possessed at least one of the MHC-I alleles Mamu-B*004:01, Mamu-B*039:01, or Mamu-A1*032:02.
source: When compared, 10 of 19 NAb non-inducers also possessed at least one of these alleles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative MHC-I genotype analysis.

claim: The possession of MHC-I alleles Mamu-B*004:01, Mamu-B*039:01, or Mamu-A1*032:02 did not significantly differ between NAb inducer and non-inducer groups.
source: This did not significantly differ with the NAb inducer group (p=0.25 by Fisher's exact test, data not shown), indicating that NAb induction was not simply linked with possession of these MHC-I genotypes but instead required furthermore specific selection of the Nef-G63E mutation (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the comparative analysis.

claim: NAb induction was not simply linked with possession of MHC-I genotypes Mamu-B*004:01, Mamu-B*039:01, or Mamu-A1*032:02 but instead required specific selection of the Nef-G63E mutation.
source: This did not significantly differ with the NAb inducer group (p=0.25 by Fisher's exact test, data not shown), indicating that NAb induction was not simply linked with possession of these MHC-I genotypes but instead required furthermore specific selection of the Nef-G63E mutation (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the statistical findings.

claim: Nef-G63E was confirmed to be an escape mutation from Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses.
source: Nef-G63E was confirmed to be an escape mutation from Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the CD8+ T-cell response analysis.

claim: NAb non-inducers possessing MHC-I alleles Mamu-B*004:01, Mamu-B*039:01, or Mamu-A1*032:02 elicited little or no Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses.
source: NAb non-inducers possessing these alleles elicited little or no Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that in vivo selection and fixation of this Nef-G63E SIV was indeed Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T cell-dependent.
evidence: This is a finding from the CD8+ T-cell response analysis in NAb non-inducers.

claim: In vivo selection and fixation of Nef-G63E SIV was Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T cell-dependent.
source: NAb non-inducers possessing these alleles elicited little or no Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that in vivo selection and fixation of this Nef-G63E SIV was indeed Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T cell-dependent.
evidence: This is an inference from the CD8+ T-cell response data.

claim: Replication of SIV carrying the Nef-G63E mutation was comparable with WT on a cynomolgus macaque HSC-F CD4+ T-cell line.
source: Replication of SIV carrying the Nef-G63E mutation was comparable with WT on a cynomolgus macaque HSC-F CD4+ T-cell line (Akari et al., 1996), excluding the possibility that the mutation critically impairs viral replication (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), and plasma viral loads were comparable between Nef-G63E mutant-selecting NAb inducers versus non-inducers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from the in vitro replication assay.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation does not critically impair viral replication.
source: Replication of SIV carrying the Nef-G63E mutation was comparable with WT on a cynomolgus macaque HSC-F CD4+ T-cell line (Akari et al., 1996), excluding the possibility that the mutation critically impairs viral replication (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), and plasma viral loads were comparable between Nef-G63E mutant-selecting NAb inducers versus non-inducers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference from the replication assay and viral load data.

claim: Plasma viral loads were comparable between Nef-G63E mutant-selecting NAb inducers versus non-inducers.
source: Replication of SIV carrying the Nef-G63E mutation was comparable with WT on a cynomolgus macaque HSC-F CD4+ T-cell line (Akari et al., 1996), excluding the possibility that the mutation critically impairs viral replication (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), and plasma viral loads were comparable between Nef-G63E mutant-selecting NAb inducers versus non-inducers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from the viral load analysis.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation did not confer notable change in downregulation of major targets CD3, CD4, MHC-I, CXCR4, and BST-2 compared with WT.
source: Nef-G63E mutation did not confer notable change compared with WT (p=not significant [n.s.] for all molecules, data not shown), implicating other non-canonical changes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from the surface molecule downregulation assay.

claim: Plasma ferritin levels showed no differences between Nef-G63E-selecting NAb inducers and non-inducers.
source: Here, plasma ferritin levels showed no differences (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and viral loads were comparable as aforementioned between Nef-G63E-selecting NAb inducers and non-inducers, arguing against gross involvement of ferritin as well as other viral replication-related Nef phenotypes at least in this model.
evidence: This is a finding from the ferritin level analysis.

claim: The findings argue against gross involvement of ferritin as well as other viral replication-related Nef phenotypes in this model.
source: Here, plasma ferritin levels showed no differences (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and viral loads were comparable as aforementioned between Nef-G63E-selecting NAb inducers and non-inducers, arguing against gross involvement of ferritin as well as other viral replication-related Nef phenotypes at least in this model.
evidence: This is an inference from the ferritin and viral load data.

claim: The threonine 308-phosphorylated Akt (pAkt Thr308) level remained unaffected by the Nef-G63E mutation.

claim: A high-MOI SIV infection accelerated phenotype appearance from day 3 to day 1 p.i., with stronger pAkt reduction.

claim: The Akt-inhibitory G63E mutant Nef phenotype is PI3K stimuli-dependent.

source: Transcriptome analysis signatured decrease in PI3K-pAkt-FoxO1-related genes in mutant SIV infection (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).

claim: Nef-G63E mutation may be T helper cell (Th)-cytopathic and decrease Th dysfunctional expansion.

source: This mutant did not associate with NAb induction in one control animal (R06-034) even upon preferential selection (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B) and Nef-G63R mutant was not similarly decreased in pAkt drive (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C), implicating that the Nef-G63E mutation was more tightly linked with NAb induction in terms of an immunosignaling phenotype.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation was more tightly linked with NAb induction in terms of an immunosignaling phenotype compared to Nef-G63R.

source: Results were biochemically confirmed by a decrease in G63E-mutated Nef binding to the mTORC2-intrinsic cofactor Sin1 in coimmunoprecipitation analysis of infected HSC-F cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a finding from the coimmunoprecipitation analysis.

source: We surmised that some targeted Nef intrusion against Env-specific B cells may be occurring and that the decreased aberrant drive of Nef-PI3K/mTORC2 may result in their enhanced maturation in lymph nodes.

claim: Nef-driven aberrant PI3K/mTORC2 signaling does occur in Nef-invaded B cells in vivo.
source: Nef invasion upregulated pAkt Ser473 (Ch 03) to a range resembling in vitro analysis (Figure 5C), demonstrating that Nef-driven aberrant PI3K/mTORC2 signaling does occur in Nef-invaded B cells in vivo.

claim: Addition of soluble, stimulation-competent antibodies against macaque CD3 enhanced adhesion of Nef+ T cells to B cells.
source: Importantly, addition of soluble, stimulation-competent antibodies against macaque CD3 enhanced adhesion of Nef+ T cells to B cells (Figure 6A, bottom center).
evidence: This is a finding from the in vitro coculture experiment.

claim: Polarized Nef protrusion/injection from T cells to B cells was readily detected in doublets.
source: In these doublets, we readily detected images of polarized Nef protrusion/injection from T cells to B cells (second column, filled wedges) as well as trogocytosed B-cell membranes (third column, open wedge), suggesting dynamic Nef acquisition by B cells.

claim: Trogocytosed B-cell membranes were detected in doublets, suggesting dynamic Nef acquisition by B cells.
source: In these doublets, we readily detected images of polarized Nef protrusion/injection from T cells to B cells (second column, filled wedges) as well as trogocytosed B-cell membranes (third column, open wedge), suggesting dynamic Nef acquisition by B cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the imaging cytometry of cocultures.

claim: An enhancement of live singlet Ramos B-cell Nef acquisition was observed by CD3 stimulation in conventional flow cytometry.
source: Substantiated by the acquired images, an enhancement of live singlet Ramos B-cell Nef acquisition (% Nef+ in total B cells) was also observed by CD3 stimulation in conventional flow cytometry (Figure 6B).

claim: There was a similar enhancement of Nef acquisition when phytohemagglutinin (PHA) was added.
source: There was a similar enhancement when we added phytohemagglutinin (PHA), whereas phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA)/ionomycin did not affect Nef acquisition by B cells.

source: There was a similar enhancement when we added phytohemagglutinin (PHA), whereas phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA)/ionomycin did not affect Nef acquisition by B cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the flow cytometry analysis of cocultures with different stimuli.

claim: Recapitulation of the decreased B-cell pAkt Ser473 phosphorylation upon G63E Nef transfer compared to that of WT Nef was detected in a 72-hour static coculture with primary CD20+ B cells.
source: In a similar 72-hour static coculture with primary CD20+ B cells, we detected recapitulation of the decreased B-cell pAkt Ser473 phosphorylation upon G63E Nef transfer compared to that of WT Nef (Figure 6C), indicating that the Nef-G63E mutation can directly alleviate maturation inhibition in preferentially Nef-targeted Env-specific B cells.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation can directly alleviate maturation inhibition in preferentially Nef-targeted Env-specific B cells.
source: In a similar 72-hour static coculture with primary CD20+ B cells, we detected recapitulation of the decreased B-cell pAkt Ser473 phosphorylation upon G63E Nef transfer compared to that of WT Nef (Figure 6C), indicating that the Nef-G63E mutation can directly alleviate maturation inhibition in preferentially Nef-targeted Env-specific B cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the coculture experiment findings.

source: NAb inducers showed significantly higher Env-specific IgG+ PB responses around week 30 p.i., after Nef-G63E selection, compared to those in NAb non-inducers (Figure 7B and C).

source: At 1 year, this difference became enhanced as a result of less pronounced decrease in Env-specific PB frequencies in the NAb inducers.
evidence: This is a finding from the temporal B-cell response analysis.

source: In NAb non-inducers, all vectors converged on an empirically defined polygonal attractor area Dn (gray area surrounded with dotted lines in Figure 7D, right) at year 1 p.i. and beyond, describing that these NAb non-inducers failed to sustain Env-specific GC output.
evidence: This is a finding from the two-dimensional vector analysis of B-cell responses.

claim: The vectors were consistently tracked outside Dn in the NAb inducers with Nef-G63E.
source: In contrast, the vectors were consistently tracked outside Dn in the NAb inducers with Nef-G63E (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a finding from the two-dimensional vector analysis of B-cell responses.

claim: At the time of NAb induction, the vectors converged on another upper-right GC output attractor area Di that is mutually exclusive with Dn.
source: At the time of NAb induction, they converged on another upper-right GC output attractor area Di (red area surrounded with dotted lines in Figure 7D, right) that is mutually exclusive with Dn (p<0.0001 by Fisher's exact test on NAb non-inducer/inducer vector distribution frequency within Dn).
evidence: This is a finding from the two-dimensional vector analysis of B-cell responses.

claim: The findings suggest more robust virus-specific IgG+ B-cell responses following Nef-G63E CD8+ T-cell escape mutant selection, ultimately leading to NAb induction.
source: These suggest more robust virus-specific IgG+ B-cell responses following Nef-G63E CD8+ T-cell escape mutant selection, ultimately leading to NAb induction.

source: The enhanced signature of cognate B cells was also an inverted pattern of impaired terminal differentiation of B-cell responses in APDS (Al Qureshah et al., 2021).

source: Taken together, in the current model, Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses in persistently SIVmac239-infected macaques selected for an escape mutant, Nef-G63E, which displays attenuated aberrant Nef binding and ensuing drive of B-cell-inhibitory PI3K/mTORC2.

source: Nef invasion of B cells in vivo occurred more preferentially in Env-specific B cells, suggesting diminution in Nef-mediated tonic dysregulation of B cells after mutant selection.
evidence: This is a summary of the key findings.

source: These events conceivably predisposed to enhanced Env-specific B-cell responses and subsequent SIVmac239-specific NAb induction, altogether, in a manner reciprocal to human APDS-mediated immune dysregulation.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the findings in the context of human disease.

source: In the present study, we found that in macaques infected with an NAb-resistant SIV, selection of a CD8+ T-cell escape nef mutant virus, Nef-G63E, precedes NAb induction.

source: As a result, Nef binding-mediated drive of PI3K/mTORC2 in Env-specific B cells becomes attenuated, which in turn unleashes maturation of antiviral B-cell responses in vivo to induce NAbs.
evidence: This is a summary of the mechanistic findings.

Thus, the current Nef-G63E-associated B-cell/NAb phenotype likely occurs in a 'reciprocal APDS-like' manner.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

source: SIVmac239 infection of macaques possessing MHC-I alleles associated with Nef-G63E mutation can be one unique platform to analyze virus–host interaction for B cell maturation leading to NAb induction.

source: The SIV Nef N-terminal unstructured region comprising Nef-G63E is not conserved in HIV-1 (Schindler et al., 2004), and beyond this model study it remains to be addressed whether a mutant HIV-1 with a similar immunosignaling-related phenotype can be obtained and how much lentiviral conservation exists for such interactions.

source: Preferential Nef transfer to Env-specific B cells (Figure 5) suggests potential involvement of polarized perturbation in cognate immune cells in vivo, which was best depicted for preferential infectivity of HIV-specific CD4+ T cells (Douek et al., 2002) and HIV condensation to the interface of DC-T-cell contacts (McDonald et al., 2003).

claim: Dysregulation of Env-specific B cells may well result from hijacking of cognate T-cell/B-cell interactions by the virus.
source: As cognate MHC class II interactions (Wülfing et al., 1998; Gitlin et al., 2014) regularly occur between HIV/SIV-specific CD4+ T cells and Env-specific B cells in GCs, dysregulation of Env-specific B cells may well result from hijacking of cognate T-cell/B-cell interactions by the virus.
